annotations.description: Force of Willing a Mox Diamond on turn 1 is a significant resource expenditure. The player must exile a blue card from hand and pay 1 life. The blue cards available to exile are Stock Up, Phyrexian Metamorph, or Force of Will itself (but FoW is being cast). Looking at the hand: City of Traitors, Island, The One Ring, Stock Up, Grim Monolith, Phyrexian Metamorph. Exiling a blue card means losing either Stock Up (card advantage) or Phyrexian Metamorph (a flexible threat/utility creature). Mox Diamond is a mana accelerant but the opponent still needs to discard a land for it. The player's own hand has a strong plan: City of Traitors + Grim Monolith enables a turn 2 The One Ring, which provides protection and card draw. Using Force of Will here 2-for-1s yourself to stop a 1-mana accelerant. While denying the opponent mana acceleration has value, the cost is steep — losing a card like Phyrexian Metamorph or Stock Up, plus 1 life. The opponent likely has other resources, and the player's own gameplan is strong enough that they may not need to Force a Mox Diamond. Saving Force of Will for a more impactful threat (like countering the opponent's key spell later) could be better.

annotations.description: Playing City of Traitors on turn 1 means that if Grk41F Stats draws and plays Island next turn (or any other land), City of Traitors will be sacrificed. With Grim Monolith and The One Ring in hand, City of Traitors enables a turn 2 Grim Monolith (City for CC, tap Monolith for CCC = 5 mana, enough for The One Ring with an additional land). However, playing Island first would preserve it permanently and still allow City of Traitors on turn 2 for the same Grim Monolith + The One Ring line without risk of losing City. Playing Island turn 1, City turn 2 gives: Island (U) + City (CC) = 3 mana for Grim Monolith, then tap Monolith for CCC, total 4 colorless available for The One Ring. Playing City turn 1 means turn 2 you play Island and sacrifice City, leaving just Island + whatever you played. The City-first line is actually worse because you lose the City when you play the Island. The optimal sequence is Island turn 1 (cast Preordain with U to dig), then City turn 2, tap both for Grim Monolith, tap Monolith for The One Ring. By playing City first, you can't cast Preordain this turn and you risk losing City next turn.
